Add a merge of channels

Source: R/add-merge.R
add_merge.Rd

Adds a merged image of several channels as a new, virtual channel. It can be placed in the layout like any other channel, e.g. a row GFP | Cy3 | merge with layout_grid(x = channel).

Usage

add_merge(montage, ..., name = "merge", colors = NULL)

Arguments

montage

A tidymontage() object.

...

Channels to merge, as bare names or strings. Use backticks or strings for names with spaces, e.g. `Alexa Fluor 488`.

name

Name of the merged channel, as it appears in the layout and in labels.

colors

Colours of member channels in this merge only, as a named vector, e.g. c(GFP = "red"). Members not named keep their channel colour (or, if that is black, their original colour).

Value

The montage with the merge step added.

Details

Merges are always drawn on a black background: each member channel is shown with its own colour and display range, and the colours are added up like light. Member channels don't need their own panels.

A channel coloured black ("#000000") is shown inverted in its own panels, as dark signal on white. A channel coloured with a colormap (lut()) is shown with its map. Merges need single colours: in a merge, such channels use their original colour from the image metadata (the color column) instead, unless colors sets one.

A merge combines the images that would share a panel apart from their channel, typically the channels of one file. Every panel of the merge needs exactly one image of each member channel.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
montage |>
  add_merge(GFP, Cy3, name = "merge")

# both channels inverted on their own; in the merge, Cy3 in its original
# colour and GFP in green
montage |>
  adjust_colors(Cy3 = "black", GFP = "black") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, GFP, colors = c(GFP = "green"))
} # }
